blockedIdentities.reason: halberg.com is live and is the brand own domain, but it serves only a landing page: a combined Flowserve-HALBERG logo, a language switch, and a two-item quick navigation pointing at the Flowserve SIHI and Flowserve sites. It publishes no product catalogue, specifications or application pages, so no HALBERG product area can be sourced first-party and a brand page would have nothing to show. The imprint names Flowserve SIHI Germany GmbH, Itzehoe, as responsible for the site; the copyright line names Halberg Maschinenbau GmbH.

profiles.shortDescription: INVpack, founded in 2003 under the name Inever, is a Spanish manufacturer of vertical form-fill-seal (VFFS) packaging machinery. It builds multilane machines for stick packs and sachets, together with baggers, capsule packaging, cartoning and end-of-line equipment such as transfers and pick and place units. Its machines are supplied to the food, dairy, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, nutritional and pet food sectors.
fullDescription: INVpack is the trading name of Ingeniería de Envasado Vertical SL, located at C/ Can Carmany 3, P.I. Nord, Argentona, 08310, Barcelona, Spain. The company's own Experiencia page states that it was founded in 2003 under the name Inever and that it is today one of the main players in the market for multilane vertical form-fill-seal (VFFS) machinery for stick packs and sachets, with its head office in Barcelona and collaborating partners in more than 50 countries through which its machines are exported.

The published range covers stick pack machinery producing three-seam sachets with central or lateral sealing, and sachet machinery producing four-seam sachets. The site names its equipment series as BY, SP, PH, PHA and MVA, and states that the machines handle powdered, granulated, liquid, pasty and solid products, with reel widths from 300 mm to 1200 mm. Beyond the filling machines the company also lists baggers, capsule packaging solutions, cartoning, and end-of-line equipment including transfers and pick and place units.

INVpack presents its solutions by sector, listing food, dairy, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, nutritional and pet food applications, and describes its approach as advanced and customised solutions focused on precision, efficiency and quality. The site is published in Spanish, English and French, and includes a customer service portal for after-sales support; the company states its philosophy as whoever buys an INVpack machine becoming part of the company.

profiles.officialName: Klima Celje, Industrija aerotermičnih naprav, d.d.
profiles.shortDescription: Klima Celje, Industrija aerotermičnih naprav, d.d. is a Slovenian manufacturer of fans and industrial ventilation equipment. Its production programme covers radial and axial fans, jet fans for tunnel ventilation, roof fans, air-handling (clima) units, air heaters, heat exchangers and smoke and heat extraction devices. The company states that it holds ISO 9001 certification, ATEX certification under Directive 2014/34/EU and an EN 12101-3 certificate for smoke and heat extraction devices.
fullDescription: The company describes itself on its English About page as follows: "KLIMA CELJE is a leading company in the industry of fan and industrial ventilation devices in Slovenia. In the period of 100 years since its incorporation, the Company has gained extensive experience in application and manufacturing of air-conditioning systems." It further states that after the declaration of Slovenia's independence the company successfully entered the competitive western markets, which are presently the destination for as much as 70 per cent of its export, and that all of the stated activities are carried out by a group of a 120 people.

The published production programme lists the manufactured range with model designations. Axial fans include the LAZ 250–315 and AVL 355–630 ranges, AVS (AVSV) 400–1600, N-AVV-D/K 630–2240, the ODT-AV, ODT-AVV, ODT-AVR, ODT-AVJ and ODT-AVJ-R types, and jet fans for longitudinal tunnel ventilation in diameters from 500 mm to 1,600 mm. Radial fans cover high-pressure types 101, 103 and 133 CV, high-pressure types with large air flows 104 and 134 CV, middle-pressure types with large air flows 105, 106, 135 and 136 CV, and the ODT-CV centrifugal fan. Roof fans are supplied in the SV series as SVH2, SVV2 and SVK2, including the explosion-proof EX SVK2 and the ODT-SVK and ODT-SVK2 smoke-extraction versions.

The programme also includes clima units of the KC series in 22 basic sizes, air heaters GNA2 with a Cu-Al heat exchanger, GNJ2 with a steel heat exchanger, the electric heater EGN and the explosion-proof EX GN A/J, and heat exchangers of the lamell type KG 28 and the spiral types RC and HC, together with systems for pneumatic transport, dust elimination, filtration and noise reduction. The company states that its team of experts is qualified to meet demands ranging from providing super-clean air in surgery halls to the extraction of high-temperature aggressive gases.

profiles.shortDescription: Croatia Pumpe Nova d.o.o. of Karlovac is the successor of Jugoturbina Pumps Works Karlovac and manufactures centrifugal pumps for marine, energy and general service applications. Its range covers 12 pump groups in 250 sizes and more than 500 different designs, with capacities from 10 to 40,000 m3/h. The CG marine pump line carries the Eureka licence the works acquired from Thune-Eureka, so its parts are interchangeable with pumps built by other producers under that licence.
fullDescription: Croatia Pumpe Nova d.o.o., based at Ul. Mala Švarča 124 in Karlovac, describes itself as the first and the largest Croatian pump manufacturer, founded in 1949. The site sets out the line of succession behind the Jugoturbina name: the works was established as Jugoturbina Pumps Works Karlovac, and in 1991, with Croatian independence, it changed its name to Croatia Pumpe Karlovac; the present company was established in 1996 and continues the same pump-manufacturing tradition. The company page adds that at the end of 2006 it became a member of one of the largest and most prospective Groups in Croatia, Strojopromet-Zagreb. According to the company, more than 70,000 different types of pumps have been produced so far, mainly for ship technologies and the process industry.

The Eureka element of the brand comes from a licence taken by the works. The company states on its services page that it brought the licence for CG pumps from Thune-Eureka in the past, so that parts of these pumps are interchangeable with parts from other producers who build pumps to the Eureka licence. The CG pump remains a catalogued product: a vertical single-stage volute pump for shipboard use, radially split with in-line suction and delivery connections, sealed by O-rings on tapered surfaces, running on grease-lubricated ball bearings with acid-resistant steel shafting, covering 5 to 250 l/s at heads of 10 to 160 m, up to 25 bar, 10 to 80 degrees C and a maximum of 3,500 rpm, and adaptable to a self-priming configuration.

The current programme is organised into marine pumps, energy pumps and general service pumps, spanning 12 pump groups in 250 different sizes and more than 500 different designs with capacities from 10 to 40,000 m3/h. Products are designed and developed in the company's own research facilities and, the services page states, all pumps are built under strict supervision and control of national and international institutions, whose marks are shown as the Croatian Register of Shipping (CRS), Bureau Veritas (BV), Lloyd's Register of Shipping (LRS), Registry of Italian Navy (RINA), American Bureau of Shipping (ABS), Germanischer Lloyd (GL), DNV and the Russian Maritime Register of Shipping (RMRS). Beyond new pumps, the company manufactures original spare parts for its full catalogue, repairs its own and third-party pumps, and runs hydraulic performance and cavitation testing, dynamic balancing, on-site installation and maintenance services and training. It has incorporated the quality and environmental management systems ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 14001:2015, both of which it states are compliant with Standard 10 CFR Appx B, the basis for the execution of work and the delivery of aggregates and spare parts for nuclear power plants, with references at NPP Krsko and NPP Paks.

profiles.shortDescription: MAHO is a German machine tool brand founded in Pfronten in 1920, which began producing machine tools for its own use in 1950. After the merger with Deckel and the 1994 merger of DMG with Gildemeister, the Pfronten site is today the location DMG MORI Pfronten GmbH within DMG MORI. The site builds milling machines, from the monoBLOCK series through to XXL machines.
fullDescription: The company that became MAHO was formed in Pfronten in 1920 through the merger of five precision engineers, who called their new, aspiring company Maho. From 1950 it produced tool machines for its own use. It quickly came to the attention of larger companies, who ordered specially customised machines from Maho, and in 1970 it therefore began to concentrate solely on this branch of business, acquired Graziano in Italy, went public and merged with Deckel; DMG then merged with Gildemeister in 1994, and today they are part of DMG MORI.

The Pfronten plant is described by its owner as a milling expert. It covers a total area of 149,000 m² with around 1,600 employees and offers the capacity for around 1,500 machines to leave the factory every year for global distribution, spanning 50 different types of machines from the versatile monoBLOCK series up to the XXL machines.

DMG MORI Ultrasonic Lasertec GmbH is also located at the site, where LASERTEC machines are developed and built for high-precision laser texturing and drilling, and where the subsidiary sets the standard in additive manufacturing of metallic components with the LASERTEC 3D series. The location additionally houses the Aerospace Excellence Center and the Die & Mold Excellence Center, offering application-specific expertise through to technological implementation within the scope of turnkey projects.

profiles.shortDescription: MEDC is one of the product lines within Eaton's hazardous area communications portfolio, part of the Crouse-Hinds Series. Together with the FHF product line it covers globally certified explosion proof signalling and alarm devices. The range includes alarm call points and audible and visual signalling devices for use in both hazardous and safe area environments.
fullDescription: MEDC is a product line within Eaton's hazardous area communications business, part of the Crouse-Hinds Series. That business is described by its owner as an established portfolio of products and systems designed especially for potentially explosive and severe atmospheres, bringing together the expertise of MEDC, FHF, HERNIS, IMCOS, Sonix and Oxalis across its fire and gas, telecommunications, PAGA and CCTV product lines. The portfolio's product lines are listed as HERNIS, Oxalis, MEDC, FHF, IMCOS, Sonix and FBT.

Within signalling, the MEDC and FHF product lines are presented as two of the most established names in harsh and hazardous signalling. The range comprises an extensive range of globally certified explosion proof signalling and alarm devices, including alarm call points and audible and visual signalling devices for use in both hazardous and safe area environments.

The signalling solutions are supplied to the oil and gas, marine, mining and industrial sectors. The hazardous area communications operation is contactable at Unit B, Sutton Parkway, Oddicroft Lane, Sutton in Ashfield, NG17 5FB, United Kingdom.

profiles.shortDescription: Nocchi is a retired Italian pump brand of Pentair, replaced by the Sta-Rite brand in Europe from 1 October 2018. It covered fresh water pumps for residential water supply and, in part, wastewater pumps, the latter moving to the Jung Pumpen brand. Pentair announced in 2018 that the successor Sta-Rite line for residential water supply and water disposal would be manufactured in Pisa, Italy; the Sta-Rite site now states that distribution of Sta-Rite products in Europe has been discontinued, with spare parts supplied within the warranty period.
fullDescription: Nocchi was an Italian pump brand within the Pentair portfolio. Pentair's European Sta-Rite site states that the former Italian pump brand Nocchi became the Sta-Rite brand from 1 October 2018, and that selected wastewater pumps previously branded Nocchi would in future be marketed under the German Jung Pumpen brand. The change followed Pentair's brand review after its May 2018 separation from its electrical division, which consolidated the portfolio around larger global premium brands.

The company stated that little would change for existing Nocchi customers: the fresh water pumps would be sold under Sta-Rite, with all marketing material — packaging, catalogues and websites — adapted accordingly. The Sta-Rite brand is described on the same site as existing since 1934 and sold in over 100 countries worldwide, with Pentair already producing a range of Sta-Rite swimming pool pumps and cleaners in Europe.

The 2018 announcement stated that the new European Sta-Rite line for residential water supply and water disposal would be manufactured in Italy, in Pisa. The site imprint names Pentair Water Italy at Via Masaccio 13, 56010 Lugnano, Pisa, VAT number 10567100150. The catalogue that succeeded the Nocchi range is organised into surface pumps, variable speed pumps, sump, sewage and effluent pumps, booster sets, firefighting equipment, pumps for open and drilled wells, special applications, pool and spa products and accessories such as control panels, expansion tanks and variable speed drives, alongside a phase out products section. The site's main page now carries the notice that distribution of Sta-Rite products in Europe has been discontinued, with spare parts supply within the warranty period handled by e-mail.

profiles.shortDescription: Gluing Tech Concept S.r.l., formerly M.A.S. Lambertoni, designs and builds industrial gluing machinery in Cairate, Italy. Its range covers Hot Melt and PUR Melt adhesive applicators, complete gluing systems, accessories, spare parts and its own process-monitoring software. The company states that its machines, mechanical parts, spare parts and accessories are made by its own production team.
fullDescription: The company's About page traces its origin to Lambertoni, a precision mechanical workshop serving demanding sectors from general mechanics to aeronautics: "La nostra storia inizia con Lambertoni, officina meccanica di precisione per i settori più esigenti, dalla meccanica all'aeronautica, ed è in questo ambito che abbiamo affinato quelle competenze tecniche che oggi ci permettono di eccellere nella progettazione e realizzazione di macchine per incollaggio Hot Melt e Pur Melt." From 2008 the business specialised in industrial gluing machines, and it later took the trading name Gluing Tech Concept S.r.l. (ex M.A.S. Lambertoni), with Marco Ferrara named on the site as CEO.

The published product range is built around Hot Melt and PUR Melt adhesive applicators, complete gluing systems, accessories and spare parts, and proprietary software. The site emphasises in-house manufacture — "Ogni macchina, ogni pezzo meccanico, ogni ricambio" comes from its own production team — and the development of proprietary technologies for process monitoring ("lo sviluppo di tecnologie proprietarie per il monitoraggio dei processi"). It also presents itself as a partner for industrial gluing offering integrated solutions and multi-brand technical support.

The company is registered at Via Ariosto 8/c, 21050 Cairate, Italy, with REA VA-312499 and a share capital of EUR 60,000 shown on the site. Sectors listed as served include food, furniture, paper converting, cosmetics, construction, electronics, sanitary/hygiene products and textiles.

profiles.shortDescription: Norman Filter Company manufactures hydraulic filter housings, filter elements and filtration systems, and states that it designs, manufactures and tests high-pressure filter housings and elements itself. Its published range covers high-pressure T-type and inline filters, medium- and low-pressure filters, spin-on and tank-top filters, and custom manifold, subsea and B31.3-compliant assemblies. The company describes itself as a family-owned AS9100 certified manufacturer serving aerospace, oil and gas, and global industrial markets.
fullDescription: Norman Filter Company states that since 1998 it has been a family owned, AS9100 certified quality manufacturer of hydraulic filter housings, elements and filtration systems for the aerospace, oil and gas, and global industrial markets. The company says it designs, manufactures and tests high-pressure filter housings and elements, and that its filters are designed and manufactured in a 60,000 sqft facility in Bridgeview, Illinois. Its site is marked AS9100 and ISO certified.

The published filtration product line is organised into high pressure T-type filters (4500 Series, 4100 Series Mini-T Type, U-115 Series Filter and 4900 Series), high pressure inline filters (4200 Series, 4300 Series and 30K Series), mobile filtration systems, medium pressure and low pressure filters, spin-on and tank-top filters, and specialty application filters including brass filters for oxygen application, flange and Grayloc hub assemblies, Nickel 200 filters, threadless filters, manifold assemblies and a B31.3 compliant filter series. The company notes that the 4200 Series mini inline filter is widely used in aerospace.

Filter elements are described as all-welded and produced in house using a proprietary manufacturing process, with woven wire mesh media for surface filtration that can be cleaned by back flushing, random metal fiber elements for high viscosity applications such as PAO fluid in radar cooling systems, and sinter-bonded stainless steel elements for low flow, low micron duties. The site also lists in-house testing capability covering proof and burst, helium leak, flow and bubble point tests, and manufacturing equipment including CNC machining, GTAW, GMAW, micro TIG, plasma and computerised orbital welding, a core tube manufacturing room, a metrology lab with CMM and optical comparator, ultrasonic tanks and a nitrogen purge oven.

profiles.shortDescription: Pavan is a manufacturer of pasta production technology and now operates as GEA Pavan within the GEA Group, which acquired the company. Its equipment covers dry and fresh pasta processing lines, extrusion dies and moulds, pasta packaging equipment, and snacks and breakfast cereals equipment. The lines also produce couscous, noodles, gluten-free pasta, ready meals, snacks and breakfast cereals.
fullDescription: The pavan.com domain now redirects to GEA's pasta pages, and GEA states that thanks to the acquisition of Pavan it has extended its presence to pasta production, one of the most popular food products present in many cultures across the world. GEA also states that with the acquisition of Pavan it introduced vacuum technology into its portfolio, advancing a solution that Pavan first brought to the market in 1956. GEA refers to the business as GEA Pavan and says the technology developed by GEA Pavan makes it possible to produce pasta of excellent quality from a variety of starch-based raw materials.

The equipment portfolio is organised into Dry Pasta Processing Equipment, Fresh Pasta Processing Equipment, Dies & Moulds, Pasta Packaging Equipment and Snacks & Breakfast Cereals Equipment. Named dry pasta lines include the GEA NexGen short-cut lines, described as engineered to simplify the process and improve overall efficiency, the long-cut Multi tier production line, the long-cut Multidrive production line, and a couscous production line. The dies and moulds range covers extrusion moulds, cutting systems and die washing machines. Drying uses the TAS (Thermo Active System) and climatic zones technology.

Output formats named on the pages include long-cut dry pasta such as spaghetti, bucatini and vermicelli, short-cut formats, nest shaped pasta, single and double sheet fresh pasta, filled products such as ravioli and tortellini, gluten-free pasta, noodles, couscous, ready meals, frozen food, snacks and breakfast cereals. GEA operates a technology center for pasta and extrusion technologies in Galliera Veneta, Italy.

profiles.shortDescription: SPECTRO Analytical Instruments manufactures instruments for elemental analysis. Its range covers ICP-OES and ICP-MS spectrometers, XRF spectrometers and handheld XRF analyzers, and mobile, portable and stationary metal analyzers based on arc/spark OES and LIBS. The instruments are used for material identification, quality control and process control in metals, mining, chemical, environmental, electronics, petroleum and polymer applications.
fullDescription: SPECTRO Analytical Instruments GmbH is a business unit of AMETEK Inc. The company states on its About Us page that it "manufactures advanced instruments and develops the best solutions for elemental analysis in a broad range of applications". According to the same page, SPECTRO was founded in 1979 and over 50,000 instruments have been delivered globally since then, ranging from handheld spectrometers used in applications such as metal recycling to fully automatic sample preparation and analysis systems for process control.

The product range is organized into six lines: ICP-OES spectrometers (SPECTRO ARCOS, SPECTROGREEN, SPECTRO GENESIS), ICP-MS spectrometers (SPECTROGREEN MS), XRF spectrometers (SPECTRO XEPOS, SPECTROCUBE, SPECTRO MIDEX, SPECTROSCOUT), handheld XRF analyzers (SPECTRO xSORT), mobile and portable metal analyzers (SPECTROTEST, SPECTROPORT) and stationary metal analyzers (SPECTROLAB S, SPECTROMAXx, SPECTROCHECK). The site describes the underlying measurement techniques it uses as ICP-OES/ICP-AES, ICP-MS, XRF, arc/spark OES and LIBS, and describes calibration features such as the iCAL and iCAL 2.0 single-sample standardization procedures.

The company groups its applications by industry, listing mining and geochemistry, metals (primary producers, foundries, semi-finished products, fabricated and finished goods, recycling, precious metals, powder metallurgy), chemical, environmental (water, waste water, soil and sludge, waste and alternative fuels), electronics including RoHS, WEEE, Li-ion batteries and solder, petroleum (crude oil, fuel, lube oil and used oil analysis), polymers, academia, geology, transportation, aerospace, automotive, agronomy, cement, food, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals. Alongside instruments SPECTRO offers repair service, parts and consumables, preventative maintenance and full service contracts, calibration service and training courses. Its imprint gives the legal entity as SPECTRO Analytical Instruments GmbH, Boschstr. 10, 47533 Kleve, Germany, registered at the Register Court Kleve under HRB 1876.

profiles.shortDescription: SHB Hebezeugbau GmbH manufactures safety-relevant components for materials handling and railway technology, including drum and disc brakes, hydraulic buffers, clutches, brake discs and drums, running wheels and wheelsets, and rope drums. Its railway programme covers locomotive traction equipment and complete buffer systems to EN 15551. The company also services, maintains, converts and repairs crane systems from its site in Saalfeld.
fullDescription: SHB Hebezeugbau GmbH states its scope on its own home page: "We manufacture individual components for railroad and conveyor technology and take care of the service, maintenance, conversion and repair of your crane systems. Everything from a single source." The company describes itself as an expert for safety-relevant parts and components in materials handling technology in addition to cranes, under the motto "MOTION MEETS SAFETY."

The conveyor technology product range published by the company comprises drum brakes, disc brakes, hydraulic buffers, clutches, brake discs, brake drums, running wheels, running wheel sets and rope drums. In railway technology, SHB offers components for train and buffer equipment: various types of locomotive traction equipment with tractive forces of 1.0 MN and 1.5 MN, hydraulic combination shock absorbers, and complete buffer systems of category C and L in accordance with EN 15551. The company states that this railway work is carried out in close cooperation with ETQ Eisenbahntechnische Anwendungen GmbH across research, development, design and testing. Its service offering covers maintenance, repair and conversion work as well as the prescribed safety inspections under German UVV rules.

On its company page SHB states that it looks back on more than 70 years of history and that its combination of modern mechanical engineering, innovative control technology and individual steel construction solutions sets standards in materials handling technology; it also states that SHB has been part of the Scheffer Group since 2018. The imprint identifies the operator as SHB Hebezeugbau GmbH, Straße der Freiheit 1, D-07318 Saalfeld, registered under HRB 514419 at the Amtsgericht Jena, with managing directors Thomas Scheffer and Lars Grünhage.

profiles.shortDescription: Tetra Pak supplies food processing equipment, filling machines and packaging materials for the food and beverage industry. Its processing range covers pasteurization, UHT treatment, homogenization, separation, mixing, blending, membrane filtration, heat exchangers and cleaning-in-place, alongside dedicated cheese, powder and ice cream equipment. Filling machines, downstream equipment and integrated production lines are supplied for dairy, cheese, juice and still drinks, plant-based products, powder, ice cream and other food categories.
fullDescription: Tetra Pak states its purpose on its own About page: "We're here to make food safe and available. It's why we provide advanced food production systems." The site describes an offering built around packaging materials and packages, processing equipment, filling machines, downstream equipment and integrated lines, together with services and factory solutions, and the About page footer carries the entity Tetra Pak International S.A. On its solutions pages the company presents itself as having "70+ years of experience" in the industry. The ownership is stated by the parent group on its own site, where Tetra Laval writes that "The Tetra Laval Group consists of three industry groups, Tetra Pak, Sidel and DeLaval, all focused on technologies and services for the efficient and sustainable production, processing, packaging and distribution of food."

The processing side of the portfolio is organised by technology on the company's solutions pages: aseptic dosing, blending, buffering, carbonisation, cleaning in place, extraction, fermentation, heat exchangers, heat pumps, homogenization, membrane filtration, mixing equipment, pasteurization, separation, standardization, sugar dissolving and treatment, and UHT treatment. Category-specific equipment is listed for cheese (curd making, blockforming, draining, pressing, string cheese making, brining), for powder (conveying, dosing, spray drying, screening) and for ice cream (freezing, filling, extrusion, moulding, wrapping). Named units include the Tetra Pak Pasteurizer D, Tetra Pak Homogenizer, Tetra Pak High Shear Mixer, Tetra Pak Continuous Freezer A2, Tetra Pak Multilane Wrapper A4 and the HighLift heat pump.

Filling equipment is published as distinct machine designations tied to package formats. Aseptic machines include E3/Speed Hyper, E3/Speed, A3/Speed, A3/CompactFlex, A3/Flex and the A1 series for Tetra Fino Aseptic, Tetra Wedge Aseptic and Tetra Classic Aseptic packages; chilled machines include E3/Flex and E3/CompactFlex, the TT/3 models for Tetra Top packages and TR/G7, TR/27 and TR/28 for Tetra Rex gable-top cartons; food machines R1 and R2 fill Tetra Recart cartons. Alongside the hardware, the site lists maintenance, service agreements and technical support, automation and digitalisation under Tetra Pak Factory OS, and product development centres serving dairy, cheese, juice, nectar and still drinks, plant-based products, powder, ice cream, New Food, other beverages and food supplement and nutrition.
